scope: source-built macOS fixed-sibling geometry Worker isolation
implementation_facts: Runtime resolves only its same-directory Worker sibling (with a Cargo test sibling exception); no MCP input chooses a path, command or environment.
macOS launch uses posix_spawn with POSIX_SPAWN_CLOEXEC_DEFAULT and only explicit stdin/stdout/stderr pipes.
The parent applies a monotonic 10-second wall-clock watchdog and kill/reap; EINTR is retried only while the same absolute deadline remains valid, and other wait errors are safely handled.

The Worker accepts exactly one bounded JSON request and returns exactly one bounded JSON response. Runtime validates protocol, request ID, cohort, program hash and strict GLB readback before persistence.
Worker CPU/core ceilings are installed before request-byte intake and stricter inherited soft limits are never raised.

A normal Worker exit is checked with Darwin wait4 peak RSS before response JSON is parsed. Any observed peak above 512 MiB is rejected before CAS/candidate persistence; this is an accepted-result budget gate, not operating-system prevention.
The closed Worker allocator has a 512 MiB accounting guard, but it does not prove operating-system total-RSS or virtual-memory enforcement.
Worker pipe descriptors use RAII ownership, so a later pipe or spawn failure closes every earlier endpoint.

host_limit_observation.cpu_seconds: verified at or below 10 seconds; stricter inherited soft limits remain effective
host_limit_observation.rlimit_rss: unavailable or advisory rather than an enforceable hard cap on observed Darwin host
host_limit_observation.accepted_peak_rss: wait4 ru_maxrss is measured in bytes and a result above 512 MiB is rejected before response parsing or persistence
host_limit_observation.conclusion: Do not claim the GeometryProgram 512 MiB budget is an OS total-memory hard cap on this platform.

coverage: truthful Darwin limits and allocator guard
EINTR deadline and pipe-failure descriptor cleanup
legacy V1 geometry, appearance and host-golden-path regressions through the isolated Worker path

limitations: The current ad-hoc Dev.app has a completed structural Worker E2E receipt: its exact packaged MCP, Runtime and same-directory Geometry Worker report matching cohort f4885b11fc54b27b88b81bb9d56b84cbd54b76a1ee5e139e531595ea57126bc1 while raw V2 geometry_prepare/readback and real Codex CLI structural paths pass. It is not a Developer ID/notarized production package or a user-restarted Desktop activation receipt.
This evidence does not prove visual similarity, PBR V2, AssetPack, high-detail operators, Viewer comparison, export/restart hash parity or complete 360-degree coverage.
